narrative.northStar: Rhodonite in Hand, kept in a specimen cabinet whose open drawer is the list
narrative.overview:
Amber is a piece of rhodonite: dense graphite stone with one pink vein running through it. In the stone's own colors, everything at rest is quiet: the page, a surface one step off it, gray words. The vein is pastel pink, and it only shows where something matters right now: the one main action, the box you just ticked, the words your search found, the thing that has focus.

The stone is kept the way minerals are, in a specimen cabinet, after the stones Amber and Rhodonite are named for. The sidebar is the cabinet's body, one step under the page, with a drawer front for each place. The drawer you choose slides out and becomes the tray you work in: on a wide screen the open drawer and the main area are one outlined surface with no seam between them, and on a phone the open place's name is a tab on top of that outlined tray. Inside the tray, a list's tasks are label slips ruled in smaller trays, names of sections are framed labels, and an achieved dream sits on a shelf as a specimen with its collection label. The cabinet lends type, density, shape and one move; navigation and controls stay the ones people already know, and the search bar is the familiar one from every list app.

It is a working surface, used daily and quickly, so density is moderate and the hierarchy is plain: a page heading, framed section labels, trays of slips. Personality lives in small tactile moments: the drawer sliding out into its tray, a round checkbox whose tick draws itself in, a dream carried from the tray onto the Achieved shelf, an Undo message that slides up from the bottom. Everything has a reduced-motion version that simply appears.

Light is entirely light and dark is entirely dark. Dark is the default (the `:root` values); light mode, chosen by the system or in Settings, is the same cabinet in daylight: pale body, white fronts and tray, graphite outlines, the pink line deepened to deep rose and focus drawn in graphite so both stay visible on white. Neither mode borrows a surface from the other.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous world per mode: no dark panel in light mode, no light panel in dark mode.
The open drawer and the tray are one surface, outlined 2px in the text color.
Graphite and off-white, with a single pink accent that always means something.
Flat surfaces separated by tone and hairline borders; shadows only on what floats.
Small corners (6px and 8px, 4px on labels): drawers, trays and plates, not pills. Round only for what's ticked.
One typeface, Plus Jakarta Sans, at a small set of sizes and weights.
Every control has an edge people can find (3:1), and every color meets level AA in both modes.

rules.name: The One Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks one kind of thing at a time: the primary action, the ticked state, the found words, or focus. It is never decoration, never a background wash, never a heading color. If a screen has two pink buttons, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Graphite-on-Pink Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite. Pastel pink is never text on a light background.

rules.name: The No Pink Category Rule
rules.body: Pink is not a category color; it would compete with focus and the main action.

rules.name: The Light Is Light Rule
rules.body: Light mode is entirely light and dark mode entirely dark (the owner's rule, 18 November 2026). No surface, drawer or chosen option is filled with the text color; the open drawer, the tray and anything chosen are marked by an outline in the text color on the surface tone.

rules.name: The Outlined Chosen Rule
rules.body: Something chosen (a segment of the Any/Open/Done switch, the kind of list or the theme, a tag on a task) keeps the surface tone and takes an outline in the text color (a 1.5px ring inside a segment; on a tag, its 1px edge plus a 1px ring inside, 2px in all and no jump in size), with semibold words; a tag also swaps its dot for a check. Pink stays for ticked, found, focused and the main action.

rules.name: The 16px on Touch Rule
rules.body: On a touch screen, fields are 16px text, or Safari zooms the page.

rules.name: The One Exception Rule
rules.body: A sync code, a recovery code and a link to the list are set in the system's monospace font, where telling a 0 from an O matters more than the typeface. Nothing else uses it.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside the tray comes from weight, framed labels and muted color, not new sizes: a section's name is a small framed label, not a bigger heading.

rules.name: The Wrap, Don't Squeeze Rule
rules.body: Rows and bars use `flex-wrap` with minimum widths in rem. At 200% text, move buttons, the Add button and the search field drop to their own line; words are never crushed.

rules.name: The 44px Finger Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every target reaches 44px, through an invisible layer around the control, so the drawing and the layout stay the same size. Drawer fronts grow to 44px.

rules.name: The Shadow Means Floating Rule
rules.body: Nothing that stays in the page's flow casts a shadow: not the cabinet, a drawer, the tray or a slip. If it has a shadow, it is modal, transient or in the hand.

dos: Do take every color from the tokens in `src/app.css`; both modes are defined there.
Do keep each mode one world: light surfaces in light mode, graphite surfaces in dark mode.
Do mark what's open or chosen with an outline in the text color (2px for the open drawer and the tray, 1.5px for a chosen option), semibold, on the surface tone.
Do keep the open drawer and the tray one outline, with no seam where they meet.
Do keep the cabinet to type, density, shape and its one move; controls stay standard.
Do keep pink to one meaning per moment, with graphite text on it and deep rose for pink lines in light mode.
Do give every control a 3:1 edge (`control-edge`) and every target 44px on touch.
Do separate surfaces by tone and hairline; add a shadow only to something that floats.
Do pair every transition with `motion-reduce` so it appears instantly instead.
Do use Tailwind classes; inline styles and `data:` URLs are blocked by the Content-Security-Policy.
donts: Don't fill a drawer, a chosen option or any surface with the text color, in either mode.
Don't split the page into a dark sidebar beside a light page, or the reverse.
Don't use pink as text on a light background, as decoration, or as a category color.
Don't use black (`#000000`) for text or surfaces; graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
Don't add a second typeface or load fonts from another domain.
Don't put shadows on the cabinet, drawers, the tray, slips or anything in the page's flow.
Don't reach for pills; the cabinet's corners are small.
Don't squeeze rows at large text; let them wrap.
Don't use category colors as fills behind text, or as a thick edge on a row or card.
Don't redraw, recolor or stretch the Itrium logo files; they are copies from the brand assets.
